articles.title: Why the Russian Exclave of Kaliningrad Is at the Center of a NATO Row
articles.summary: The Russian exclave of Kaliningrad on the Baltic Sea has the potential to become a flashpoint with NATO as recent maritime security incidents between Russia and Ukraine bring renewed attention to the territory nestled between two NATO members. Moscow on Monday announced the allocation of approximately 47 billion rubles (around $572 million) toward the construction of two railway ferries between the Russian mainland and Kaliningrad, which sits between Poland and Lithuania. articles.title: How to Have a More Sustainable Black Friday, According to Experts
articles.summary: Black Friday is here—holding the promise of good deals and the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season. But if you plan to shop the sales, take the time to think about what you really need —and what you plan to give. Americans spent $10 billion dollars on unwanted gifts in 2024. And last year, 65% of consumers reported returning a holiday gift, while 54% admitted to regifting an unwanted item. articles.title: Why You Should Train to Be Ethically Fit
articles.summary: Think of great athletes; they are fit in a way that relies on years of training and practice. articles.title: What Democrats’ Sweeping Midterm Wins Could Mean for the Redistricting Battle
articles.summary: Republicans and Democrats in several states engaged in a bitter fight to redraw congressional maps in their parties’ favor leading up to this year’s midterms. But in the aftermath of the blue wave that swept across the country, that conflict may be dying down—at least for now. Typically, maps are redrawn after the results of the U.S. census are released each decade, in order to account for population and demographic changes.
